title: Echelon GPU Systems x Redwood Intro & Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery call between Redwood and Echelon GPU Systems to explore partnership for co-selling Dedicated and Private deployment options. Discussed Echelon's hardware footprint, integration possibilities (bare metal, VPC peering, on-prem appliance), target customers, compliance needs, and next steps to share benchmarks and a joint go-to-market brief.
action_items: Marcus - share benchmark template + perf spreadsheet by 2026-11-26
Lena - send partner one-pager and sample contract language by 2026-11-25
Priya - provide inventory of target customers and regions by 2026-11-30
Omar - share rack and networking constraints doc by 2026-11-27
next_steps: Schedule technical deep-dive with Echelon infra team (SE-led) — target week of 2026-11-30
Run quick micro-benchmark on Echelon A100 nodes using Redwood dedicated runtime (Marcus to own)
Prepare a joint partner brief for sales enablement — Lena to draft
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Echelon Partnerships), Daniel Cho (Echelon Cloud Solutions), Omar Haddad (Echelon SE)
Shared links: partner deck (drive link), benchmark template (sheet link), redwood security FAQ (link)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, AE on the partnerships program at Redwood. Marcus is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing over at Echelon?
[00:05] Priya Sharma: Good, thanks Lena. Excited to kick this off, we've been following Redwood's infra work.
[00:10] Daniel Cho: Hi all, thanks for setting this up. Quick note we have a hybrid team in US and EU so interested in region coverage.
[00:15] Marcus Hill: Awesome. Quick agenda — intros, high level goals for partnership, tech constraints (hardware, networking), compliance, and then next steps / benchmarks. Sound good?
[00:20] Omar Haddad: Yep, that's good.
[00:25] Priya Sharma: Works.

[02:12] Lena Ortiz: To kick off, what's Echelon's main business focus now? Are you pursuing dedicated cloud resale, appliance, fully managed private deployments?
[02:18] Daniel Cho: We're mainly a GPU hardware + managed infra provider. We build racks with mixes of A100 and H200 variants and sell to enterprises that need predictable throughput. Lately we've had more inbound about managed private deployments — customers asking for co-managed stacks.
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: Great. That maps well to Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private. Marcus, quick context on how our Dedicated offering works?
[02:36] Marcus Hill: Sure. Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with our inference runtime; customers get predictable throughput and we can co-locate it on partner hardware in some cases. We also support our Private deployment which can run inside a customer VPC or on-prem with our control plane shims. Important details are network latency, whether you want VPC peering or direct connect, and disk encryption/KMS integration.
[02:54] Priya Sharma: On the networking question, Echelon often does cross-connects and direct fiber into customer DCs — we can do private link or transit but need to understand requirements. Also some customers want the appliance model where they actually host the box.

[05:00] Marcus Hill: For appliance/on-prem we usually need a lightweight agent and some port openings for the control plane. For fully air-gapped installs we have an on-prem bundle but that's heavier. It's helpful to know the typical rack-level power and cooling constraints — any of that documented?
[05:18] Omar Haddad: We have a rack spec sheet — I'll share it. Some customers limit outbound connectivity, which is when our on-prem bundle comes into play.

[07:40] Daniel Cho: A few technical questions from our infra folks — what's the runtime dependency on NVIDIA stack versions? Catalyst, driver versions, CUDA?
[07:47] Marcus Hill: Good question. Our runtime supports CUDA 12.x and 11.8 for older kernels; we do kernel-level optimizations for attention and KV cache. There are recommended driver versions per model. For H200 there are a few hotspots — we can surface a compatibility matrix.
[08:05] Lena Ortiz: We should send the compatibility matrix after the call.

[09:50] Priya Sharma: From a commercial angle, Echelon can present Redwood as a supported option in our partner portal, but we need MOUs on support SLAs and joint pricing. Any standard partner contract?
[10:00] Lena Ortiz: Yes we have partner one-pagers and sample SOW language — I'll share. For SLAs, Dedicated customers usually expect 99.x uptime and defined latency SLOs; we can discuss co-support models.

[12:30] Marcus Hill: On benchmarking — we recommend microbenchmarks for latency (p95/p99), throughput with batching, and memory/kv hit ratios. We have a benchmark template — we'll run an initial test on your A100 fleet.
[12:45] Omar Haddad: Great, our ops team can stand up a test node. Do you need sample prompts or workload types?
[12:50] Marcus Hill: Yes, ideally a representative prompt set and seq lengths. Many enterprise LLM workloads are 512-2k tokens; caller patterns determine batching.

[15:00] Daniel Cho: Security/compliance is a big one. Our customers often require SOC2 or ISO attestations, SSO integration, RBAC — do you have those?
[15:08] Lena Ortiz: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC at route/model levels, and KMS integrations (customer-managed keys). We'll share our security FAQ and SOC2 report under an NDA.

[17:22] Priya Sharma: Data residency — some EU customers require data not leave region, and others want no telemetry stored. Can Redwood support region pinning and data retention exports?
[17:32] Marcus Hill: Yes; on Hosted we offer region selection. For Dedicated/Private, data stays in customer environment and we can configure retention and audit logs. We also have audit logging that can be shipped to a customer SIEM.

[20:10] Omar Haddad: A practical question — what's typical network egress for 1k qps with 4k token average? Just want to estimate bandwidth and inter-node KV sync traffic.
[20:18] Marcus Hill: That depends a lot on batching and prefix caching. Rough back-of-envelope: 1k qps at 4k tokens is large — we usually advise batching and KV cache to lower per-token overhead. We'll validate with the benchmark.

[22:45] Lena Ortiz: Thinking about GTM — we envision co-sell where Echelon surfaces Redwood as a recommended inference runtime for customers buying your racks, and Redwood references Echelon as a certified partner for Dedicated deployments. Would that match your priorities?
[22:55] Priya Sharma: Yes, that's attractive. We also want joint marketing collateral and maybe a field enablement session.

[24:30] Daniel Cho: On pricing, do you do reseller margins or referral fees?
[24:36] Lena Ortiz: We have flexible partner programs — referral credits, reseller discounts for committed capacity, and co-sell incentive structures. We'll share the partner program doc.

[27:05] Omar Haddad: Any blocker for a quick pilot? We could host a small 4-GPU cluster and let Redwood run the runtime for a two-week pilot.
[27:12] Marcus Hill: That sounds doable. We'll need access details, driver versions, and a test workload. Marcus to coordinate the perf runs.

[30:00] Priya Sharma: A few admin items — who will be the support contact if a customer raises an infra issue versus app-level issue?
[30:07] Lena Ortiz: Usually first-line is Echelon as infrastructure owner, then Redwood handles runtime/inference-specific escalations. We can agree on escalation matrix in the MOU.

[33:40] Daniel Cho: For Private deployments we noticed some customers have strict key management — HSM requirement. Does Redwood integrate with KMS/HSM?
[33:46] Marcus Hill: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations via standard APIs. We'll include a KMS integration doc.

[36:00] Priya Sharma: Any callouts on observability? Customers want per-route latency, token cost attribution, and traces that map to requests.
[36:07] Marcus Hill: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, model dashboards, and tracing hooks to tie back to request IDs. We can expose metrics to your monitoring stack via Prometheus or push to your SIEM.

[39:30] Omar Haddad: A nit — do you support model quantization and which quantized binaries are supported on A100/H200?
[39:36] Marcus Hill: We support quantization-friendly execution paths; we can run int8 on some model families but need to validate per-model. We'll include a quantization compatibility note in the matrix.

[42:10] Lena Ortiz: Sounds like there are a few concrete next steps — Marcus will own the perf template and run a pilot, Lena will send partner docs and program info, Omar will share rack specs and constraints, Priya will share target customers and regions.
[42:20] Priya Sharma: Correct. We'll also want a technical deep-dive next week with our infra folks.

[45:00] Daniel Cho: Any red flags so far? Latency SLA expectations, support models, or anything we should hammer out before a pilot?
[45:06] Marcus Hill: Nothing major. Need to confirm network topology to avoid cross-region latency. Also we should align on model families to test — e.g., LlamaX / open models vs transformer-based proprietary models.

[48:30] Lena Ortiz: We may also do an initial white-box perf run using a small open model to validate runtime and kernel behavior. That helps identify kernel choices and batching configs.

[50:10] Omar Haddad: One last thing — some customers use Kubernetes, others run bare-metal. How do you integrate with K8s?
[50:18] Marcus Hill: For K8s we have an operator for scheduling inference pods and autoscaling. For bare-metal we run as a system service with an orchestration shim. Both are supported but ops diffs exist.

[53:00] Lena Ortiz: Great. We'll capture action items and follow up. Thanks everyone for the time.
[53:10] Priya Sharma: Thanks Lena, Marcus — looking forward to the docs and pilot.
[53:15] Daniel Cho: Thanks all.
[53:20] Omar Haddad: Thanks.

End of transcript.
Notes: Transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., driver vs diver) and shorthand. Refer to shared links for full compatibility matrix and benchmark template.
